source.method: Cycle 34 frozen technical-document sections; retain heading plus a whitespace-bounded excerpt at most 512 UTF-16 code units. Repetitions are labeled and are not independent real documents.
source.limits: Single English technical self-documentation corpus, repeated excerpts and deterministic synthetic lexical controls; no representative traffic or relevance-quality claim.

method: Same installed production engine, captured normal configuration/default limits and public facade operations. Private queued zero-clock host drains non-deadline tasks. No real wall/CPU/deadline/fairness claim.

Registration and effect contracts

`createRaveldex({ schema, analyzer?, limits?, addons? })` accepts an explicit ordered list of trusted capability registrations. The owner validates the complete set before creating an engine: duplicate IDs, missing requirements, conflicting providers, incompatible versions, dependency cycles, and incompatible execution support reject creation. Input list order cannot change semantics; validated dependency order governs preparation only.

Each registration has a data

Admission and concurrent calls

`createRaveldex` returns an empty engine with revision 0. Each public operational call synchronously captures bounded input structures/primitive values and performs cheap shape/type/length checks before returning its promise; validation exceptions are converted into promise rejections. Source mapping

Token ranges refer to the entire original token. They are sufficient for token occurrences and original-source phrase evidence. They do not constitute a character-by-character normalization map. A prefix match initially highlights the entire matching original token; a shorter normalized prefix is not converted into a fabricated shorter original range.

Array indices are original indices, including empty values. Positions reset to zero for each value. Ranges are local to the identified
